title: Rigveda 4.47: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.47: To Vayu or Indra and Vayu: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.47 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Vayu or Indra and Vayu. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 307v-308r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.47.1-3 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 307v
translation.original_text:
1vāyo̍ śu̱kro a̍yāmi te̱ madhvo̱ agra̱ṁ divi̍ṣṭiṣu | ā yā̍hi̱ soma̍pītaye spā̱rho de̍va ni̱yutva̍tā ||
2indra̍ś ca vāyav eṣā̱ṁ somā̍nām pī̱tim a̍rhathaḥ | yu̱vāṁ hi yantīnda̍vo ni̱mnam āpo̱ na sa̱dhrya̍k ||
3vāya̱v indra̍ś ca śu̱ṣmiṇā̍ sa̱ratha̍ṁ śavasas patī | ni̱yutva̍ntā na ū̱taya̱ ā yā̍ta̱ṁ soma̍pītaye ||
translation.text:
1Vâyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites. Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God, longed-for, on thy team-drawn car.
2O Vâyu, thou and Indra are meet drinkers of these Soma-draughts, For unto you the drops proceed as waters gather to the vale.
3O Indra-Vâyu, mighty Twain, speeding together, Lords of Strength, Come to our succour with your team, that ye may drink the Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 307v (numbered 116v by the scribe) (OPenn image 308, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.46.5 ‹-indravāyūiti iha ā gatam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 308r (numbered 117r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.47.4 ‹yajña-vāhasā indravāyūiti ni yacchatam›. Verses 4.47.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1vāyo iti | śukraḥ | ayāmi | te | madhvaḥ | agram | diviṣṭiṣu | ā | yāhi | soma-pītaye | spārhaḥ | deva | niyutvatā
2indraḥ | ca | vāyo iti | eṣām | somānām | pītim | arhathaḥ | yuvām | hi | yanti | indavaḥ | nimnam | āpaḥ | na | sadhryak
3vāyo iti | indraḥ | ca | śuṣmiṇā | sa-ratham | śavasaḥ | patī iti | niyutvantā | naḥ | ūtaye | ā | yātam soma-pītaye

translation.original_ref: RV 4.47.4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 308r
translation.original_text: <sup>4</sup>yā vā̱ṁ santi̍ puru̱spṛho̍ ni̱yuto̍ dā̱śuṣe̍ narā | a̱sme tā ya̍jñavāha̱sendra̍vāyū̱ ni ya̍cchatam ||
translation.text: <sup>4</sup>The longed-for teams which ye possess, O Heroes, for the worshipper, Turn to us, Indra-Vâyu, ye to whom the sacrifice is paid.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 308r (numbered 117r by the scribe) (OPenn image 308, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.47.4 ‹yajña-vāhasā indravāyūiti ni yacchatam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 308v (numbered 117v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.49.2 ‹-pītaye›. Verse 4.47.4 ends on this page; 4.47.4 begins on fol. 307v (numbered 116v by the scribe).
